properties.name: Whether intent has been delivered is computed from the golden thread, never asserted
properties.statement: A requirement's completion must be derived from evidence already in the graph — something satisfies it, and that capability is realized and its check passes — not set by hand on the requirement itself. A hand-set "done" is a claim that outlives the truth: it survives the capability regressing, the artifact drifting, the verification starting to fail, and it degrades exactly as silently as an unreconciled checksum. Derived completion also makes the reverse question answerable without anyone maintaining it: what fraction of accepted intent is actually delivered, and which requirements are believed-done on evidence that no longer holds. The same rule applies to the rest of the lifecycle: a requirement that stopped being satisfied must be able to say so, rather than remaining green because nobody revisited it.
